text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Norway has signed its first gas supply contract with Italy. The gas negotiating committe (GFU), led by Statoil, has agreed with Italian gas company SNAM to deliver six billion cubic metres of gas per year for 25 years. At current prices, the overall value of the contract is about 90 billion crowns.

- Norway's ambassador in Sweden, Ketil Boerde, is concerned about the Swedes' negative image of Norwegians. Boerde says the Swedes see Norwegians as fools who just happen to earn a lot of money because they have oil.
- Oil and Energy Minister Ranveig Froeiland has presented new estimates for Norwegian oil production under which output will rise by 20 percent in a few years to 3.7 billion barrels a day.

- Marianne Andreassen, state secretary in the Finance Ministry, says the governemnt may change the petroleum funds's investment strategy and take bigger risks. In the National Budget the petroleum fund is estimated to hold 270 billion crowns by the end of year 2000.

- Simen Revold, head of information in Scandinavian Airline System (SAS) Norge, says SAS has sold four percent more tickets compared with the same period last year, in spite of a travel agencies' boycott of SAS. The travel agencies are protesting against SAS cutting their commission.
